prediction.likelyOutcome: Plaintiffs are likely to prevail on liability given the strong actual-notice and employee-causation evidence, with a probable total verdict (specials, general damages, and consortium) landing in the low-to-mid six figures; Walmart's comparative-fault defense will likely reduce but not eliminate recovery, and the now-lifted $75,000 cap removes the main downside constraint, while Walmart's unaccepted $101,000 statutory offer creates fee-shifting exposure if the verdict falls below $126,250.

outcome.description: The jury awarded the plaintiffs $300,000; the trial court denied Walmart's motion for JNOV (to cut the award to $75,000 under the federal remand order) or new trial. The Court of Appeals affirmed on March 12, 2024, holding the trial court did not abuse its discretion in declining to apply judicial estoppel. The opinion notes no judgment had yet been entered on the verdict. No attorney's fees.
